newsitem.title: CHINA: Quake shakes eastern China, no casualties reported.
newsitem.headline: Quake shakes eastern China, no casualties reported.

text.p: An offshore earthquake measuring 6.1 on the Richter scale shook the Yellow Sea near eastern China's Shanghai city on Saturday, but no one was reported hurt, a State Seismological Bureau official said.
"Currently, there's no (report of) damage or injuries whatsoever," the official said. "There shouldn't be any, because it was 100-200 km (60-125 miles) from the coast."
The earthquake struck at 9.56 p.m. (1356 GMT), with an epicentre at 31.7 degrees north latitude, 123.1 east longitude the official said.

There was no danger of any tsunami (tidal waves) from the tremor, which was felt in Shanghai, China's biggest city, and areas of neighbouring Jiangsu and Zhejiang provinces, he said but gave no details.
Scientists say China is passing through a period of high seismological activity.
In September, a tremor injured 17 people in southwestern Yunnan province's Lijiang county, where at least 304 people were killed in February by an earthquake measuring 7.0 on the Richter scale.
